task: Write one sentence of your own using the word acclaim. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know acclaim should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her debut poetry collection, printed by a tiny press, gathered such acclaim that bookstores could not keep it shelved.
Approval is a passing grade — a nod that the work is acceptable; acclaim is far louder and warmer than that.
Praise stops a step short of acclaim: one reviewer praises; when every reviewer praises at once, the chorus is acclaim.

Admiration is the respectful, warm feeling an audience has for good work, and it can stay entirely private — you can admire a poet and never say so. Acclaim is that feeling made loud and public: many voices praising at once, out where everyone can hear it.

Renown is the state of being widely known — a name that travels far beyond its own field. Acclaim is the praise itself, not the being known: a scientist can enjoy renown while rivals dispute her every finding, but acclaim exists only where the reviews are warm.
